item.title: Osoday 2027
item.description: Back in 2024 I was asked to give a talk for the back then online only Open Source Observability Day. While I`m not a big fan of online only events, there really was a gap that needed to be filled. Sure, we have OSMC, there used to be Monitorama which happened iirc 2x in Europe, and there is the (close to impossible to attend) o11yday before Kubecon. But there is no event where the Open Source observabilty community meets. While chatting with Peter Zaitsev about Coroot, I already hinted that maybe we could do an in person OSoday in Ghent as a Fringe event to CfgMgmtCamp. It would be an ideal fit as a number of people with this interest would already be around for Fosdem or CfgMgmtCamp so it would be only one trip for multiple events .

item.title: Cfgmgmtcamp 2027
item.description:
We are halfway 2026 already so it is time to think about what you will be doing next February.

Start with blocking your calendar for 1-3 February . As usual we’ll be meeting in Ghent for 3 days of Infrastructure Automation Geekery. It will be a fun mix of 2 days of conference with new and old communities, followed by a day of workshops hackathons and tutorials. You know you can’t mis this.

item.title: Lies, Damn Lies and Statistics, 2016 Edition
item.description:
When people sign up for Configuration Management Camp, we ask them what community room they are mostly interested in.
We ask this question because we have rooms in different sizes and we don’t want to put communities with 20 people showing interest in a 120 seat room and we don’t want to put a community with 200 people in a 60 seat room.

But it also gives us to opportunity to build some very interesting graph over the potential evolution of the communities.
